To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the energy footprint of a household is strongly linked with its level of well-being, and that the transition from inefficient traditional fuels to modern fuels, such a gas and electricity, is an important driver of well-being, but also that collective systems, such as access to health centers and public transport, and having access to sanitation and solid shelter, are more important than individual energy consumption for the attainment of basic well-being.
households with low energy use and high levels of well-being are found in all countries and that this pattern can be linked to a transition to efficient modern fuels.

the level of household final energy consumption and composition are not the most important factors in the attainment of well-beings, but rather the collective provisioning systems in terms of access to public transport, health centers, markets, and waste management, and the household characteristics such as having solid shelter, sanitation, and minimum housing space.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interconnections between the achievement of basic well-being and energy use at the household level.
the interlinkages between household energy use and the attainment of basic well-being outcomes, and their implications for SDG achievement.
the interconnections between energy use and well‐being, and their links to the achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the achievement of SDGs 1–5, 13 and 15 is possible with a low level of household energy use.
a household energy footprint is not an indicator of well-being, and the link between the two is not straightforward.
energy use and energy poverty reduction are important for the attainment and maintenance of well-being, but not the only drivers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
households with high well-beings show much higher energy efficiency and reduced environmental impacts.
households with high well-beings are those with high access to public provisioning systems and low energy use for residential fuel.
the achievement of well‐being at a low level energy use is possible, and it is associated with synergies with other SDGs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the energy transition towards efficient and sustainable energy sources is an important driver of SDG attainment.
the achievement of SDG7 can be an important enabler of SDG achievement.
the achievement of basic human well-being can be achieved with a much smaller energy footprint, thus providing a pathway to achieve the SDGs at a low level energy use and with low emissions.
